Riley: Heads up — hitting p95 latency regressions in us-west-2 serving pool 3. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/rt/us-west-2/pool-3
Riley: p50 ~ 90ms, p95 jumped from 130ms -> 420ms over the last 10m, queued_requests=84, admission_rejects=416, avg_batch_size=14.8, configured max_batch_tokens=4096
deploy-bot: alert: inference.latency.p95 > 300ms for 5m (us-west-2 / pool-3)
Tom: Do we have recent kernel/logs from the batcher? Can you paste admission counters from /metrics/admin or run `curl -s http://pool-3-admin:9100/metrics | grep admission`
Riley: pasted counters: `admission_requests_total 12543`, `admission_allowed_total 12127`, `admission_rejected_total 416`, `current_queue_depth 84`, `avg_wait_ms 87`, `max_batch_size_observed 16`
Aisha: Looks like the max-batch token guardrail is kicking in and admission is throttling under tail concurrency. Likely combination of longer sequences + few large-model requests causing KV pressure.
Tom: Can you confirm sequence length distribution? If sequences spiked, batcher might be packing fewer requests per GPU and hitting max token budget per batch. Any recent rollout?
Riley: seq_len p50=96, p90=640, p99=2048 (saw a bump around 15:03 UTC). No model rollout in last 6h. Traffic shift from partner X testing longer contexts.
Carla: Impact on customers? Is this causing errors or just slower responses?
Riley: Mostly latency right now. No surge in 5xx yet, but some client-side timeouts at 10s increased by ~0.3% over baseline. Partner X noticed slower chat replies.
Tom: Short-term mitigation options: 1) temporarily lower max_batch_tokens to 3072 or reduce max_concurrency_per_gpu, 2) enable a short-sequence fast-path (if available), 3) temporarily route partner X to a dedicated lower-latency pool in another region. Which is fastest?
Aisha: Easiest immediate change is lowering max_batch_tokens to 3072 via the runtime config. That will reduce per-batch token packing and lower queueing tail. Tradeoff: slight throughput loss and higher cost per-token.
Tom: I'll push the config change now. Command: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' http://pool-3-admin:9100/config -d '{\"max_batch_tokens\":3072}'`
Tom: API responded: `\{\"status\":\"ok\",\"applied\":{\"max_batch_tokens\":3072}}`
oncall-bot: action: config change applied to pool-3 at 2026-03-18T15:24:40Z by Tom
Riley: After change: p95 dropped to ~210ms within 90s, queued_requests down to 28, admission_rejects to 102. Client timeouts back to baseline in last 6m.
Carla: Thanks — status update I can send to partner? Short note acknowledging we throttled batching guardrail and applied config change?
Riley: Yes — tell them we applied runtime tuning to reduce batch token packing to stabilize latency, investigating long term solution.
Aisha: Long-term actions we agreed: 1) dynamic per-model batch-token limits, 2) admission token scaler based on observed seq_len distribution, 3) isolate noisy tenants (partner X) into dedicated pool or rate-limit at edge. Filed ENG-3912 for follow-up.
Tom: Also adding a test to our perf harness to simulate p99 seq lengths and ensure guardrails don't cause p95 regressions.
Riley: Marking incident resolved for now, will monitor. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: incident resolved (mitigated) at 2026-03-18T15:31:29Z
Aisha: Follow-up owners: Tom -> ENG-3912 (dynamic batching), Ops -> triage partner routing, Riley -> monitor/rollback plan. Ticket: https://tickets.internal/ENG-3912 :thumbsup:
Tom: Thanks all. Keeping alerts on 5m and 15m p95; will reopen if it reappears.
